class Fetch_ADE(instrument, data_handler)[source]¶

Bases: object

The Fetch commands retrieve analog demodulation measurement results.

__init__(instrument, data_handler)[source]¶
am(metrics)[source]¶

Fetch AM demodulation metrics.

AM? returns AM demodulation metrics. The integer parameter specifies the metric to retrieve. Possible integer values: 1. Carrier frequency in Hz 2. Carrier power in dBm 3. AM modulation rate in Hz 4. AM Depth (RMS) as % 5. AM Depth (Peak+) as % 6. AM Depth (Peak-) as % 7. AM SINAD as dB 8. AM THD as % Can specify a list of metrics to request as a comma separated list. The metrics will be returned as a comma separated list in the order they were requested.

Parameters:

metrics (int or list of int) – Metric(s) to retrieve for AM demodulation.

Returns:

Comma separated list of metric values in order requested.

Return type:

str

fm(metrics)[source]¶

Fetch FM demodulation metrics.

FM? returns FM demodulation metrics. The integer parameter specifies the metric to retrieve. Possible integer values: 1. Carrier frequency in Hz 2. Carrier power in dBm 3. FM modulation rate in Hz 4. FM Depth (RMS) in Hz 5. FM Depth (Peak+) in Hz 6. FM Depth (Peak-) in Hz 7. FM SINAD as dB Can specify a list of metrics to request as a comma separated list. The metrics will be returned as a comma separated list in the order they were requested.

Parameters:

metrics (int or list of int) – Metric(s) to retrieve for FM demodulation.

Returns:

Comma separated list of metric values in order requested.

Return type:

str

disable_iqinversion()[source]¶

Disable IQ swap compensation.

When disabled, the I and Q channels are not swapped.

disable_iqoffset()[source]¶

Disable IQ offset removal.

When disabled, IQ offset is not removed from the signal.

disable_linear_amp_error_correction()[source]¶

Disable linear amplitude error correction (ADRoop).

When disabled, linear amplitude errors are not corrected.

enable_iqinversion()[source]¶

Enable IQ swap compensation.

When enabled, the I and Q channels are swapped in the signal.

enable_iqoffset()[source]¶

Enable IQ offset removal.

When enabled, IQ offset is removed from the signal.

enable_linear_amp_error_correction()[source]¶

Enable linear amplitude error correction (ADRoop).

When enabled, linear amplitude errors are corrected for in the signal.

True if IQ swap is enabled, False otherwise.

True if amplitude droop compensation is enabled, False otherwise.

disable()[source]¶

Disable equalization.

Disables the equalization filter in digital demodulation mode.

Enable equalization.

Enables the equalization filter in digital demodulation mode.

get_convergence()[source]¶

Query the adaptive rate (convergence) of the equalizer.

Returns:

Adaptive rate (convergence).

get_length()[source]¶

Query the length of the equalization filter in symbols.

Returns:

Length of the equalization filter in symbols.

is_enabled()[source]¶

Query if equalization is enabled.

Returns:

True if equalization is enabled, False otherwise.

is_hold_enabled()[source]¶

Query if hold (bypass adaptation) is enabled.

Returns:

True if hold is enabled, False otherwise.

reset()[source]¶

Reset the equalization filter.

Resets the equalization filter to the unit impulse response (pass through).

set_convergence(value)[source]¶

Set the adaptive rate (convergence) of the equalizer.

Higher values adapt faster but are more unstable.

Parameters:

value – Adaptive rate (convergence).

set_hold_state(state)[source]¶

Enable or disable hold (bypass adaptation).

When enabled, adaptation step is bypassed but equalization is still applied.

Parameters:

state – 1/0 or ‘ON’/’OFF’ to enable/disable hold (bypass adaptation).

set_length(value)[source]¶

Set the length of the equalization filter in symbols.

The length must be an odd integer.

Parameters:

value – Length of the equalization filter in symbols (must be odd).

fetch(metrics)[source]¶

Fetch digital demodulation metrics. The integer parameter specifies the metric to retrieve. Possible integer values can be printed with function print_fetch_options(). Can specify a list of metrics to request as comma separated list. The metrics will be returned as a comma separated list in the order they were requested.

Parameters:

metrics – Metric(s) to retrieve.

Returns:

Comma separated list of metric values in order requested.

Print available fetch options for digital demodulation metrics.

List of (ID, Description) tuples for available metrics.

class IQ(instrument, data_handler)[source]¶

Bases: object

The IQ commands configure and query custom IQ constellation data.

__init__(instrument, data_handler)[source]¶
get_data()[source]¶

Returns the constellation symbols as a comma separated list of alternating IQ values.

Returns:

The constellation symbols as a comma separated list of alternating IQ values.

get_length()[source]¶

Returns the number of symbols in the custom constellation.

Returns:

The number of symbols in the custom constellation.

is_valid()[source]¶

Returns 1 when the custom constellation is valid.

Returns:

True if the custom constellation is valid, False otherwise.

set_data(iq_values)[source]¶

Specify the constellation symbols as IQ values. IQ values are specified as comma separated real numbers, alternating IQ values. If an odd number of real values are provided the last value is ignored. If any value is an invalid real number, the command fails and throws a system error. While not strictly necessary, it is suggested to scale the constellation so that the maximum symbol magnitude is 1.

Parameters:

tuple) (iq_values (list or) – List of real numbers, alternating I/Q values.

abort()[source]¶

Abort any calibration or measurement in progress. Corresponding data is not retained.

get_calibration_state()[source]¶

Returns the current calibration state for noise figure measurements.

Possible values: - ‘uncal’: No valid calibration stored. High measurement error is likely unless the DUT has at least 30 dB gain. - ‘semical’: A valid calibration is stored, but measurement accuracy is reduced due to configuration changes since last calibration. - ‘cal’: A valid calibration is stored and settings are identical to the current configuration.

Returns:

The current calibration state (‘uncal’, ‘semical’, or ‘cal’).

The next action user needs to take before continuing measurement.

set_offset_start(freq)[source]¶

Specify the start frequency of the phase noise sweep as an offset from the detected carrier center frequency.

Values must be between 10Hz and 10kHz and will be clamped to the closest value from the list [10Hz, 100Hz, 1kHz, 10kHz].

Values must be between 1kHz and 10MHz and will be clamped to the closest value from the list [1kHz, 10kHz, 100kHz, 1MHz, 10MHz].

freq – Stop frequency of the phase noise sweep as an offset from the detected carrier center frequency in Hz.

Bases: object

The Sweep Configuration commands control the sweep configuration in scalar network analysis mode.

__init__(instrument, data_handler)[source]¶
get_points()[source]¶

Query the suggested sweep size.

The final sweep size may differ due to hardware limitations.

Returns:

The suggested sweep size.

get_type()[source]¶

Query the sweep type.

Indicates whether an active or passive device is being measured.

Returns:

The sweep type.

is_hrange_enabled()[source]¶

Query if high range is enabled.

When enabled, sweep is optimized for dynamic range with a 20dB pad store through, but sweep speed will decrease.

Returns:

True if high range is enabled, False otherwise.

set_hrange(state)[source]¶

Enable or disable high range.

If high range is enabled, the software will optimize the sweep for dynamic range when a 20dB pad store through is performed. Sweep speed will decrease when selected.

Parameters:

state – 1/0 or ‘ON’/’OFF’ to enable/disable high range.

set_points(num_points)[source]¶

Specify a suggested sweep size.

The final sweep size takes this setting into consideration as well as hardware limitations when determining the final sweep size.

Parameters:

num_points – Suggested sweep size.

set_type(typ)[source]¶

Specify whether an active or passive device is being measured.

This will affect the attenuation and gain used during the sweep. Failure to properly set this value may result in reduced dynamic range or IF overload.

Parameters:

typ – ‘PASSive’ or ‘ACTive’.

get_function()[source]¶

Controls how the VBW processing is performed. If ‘AVERAGE’, overlapping FFTs are averaged together. If ‘MINMAX’, overlapping FFTs are min/max held. ‘MIN’ or ‘MAX’ returns only one of the resulting arrays.

The current detector function.

set_function(func)[source]¶

Controls how the VBW processing is performed. If ‘AVERAGE’, overlapping FFTs are averaged together. If ‘MINMAX’, overlapping FFTs are min/max held. ‘MIN’ or ‘MAX’ returns only one of the resulting arrays.

Controls the units in which the detector function is performed in.

units – ‘POWER’, ‘SAMPLE’, ‘VOLTAGE’, or ‘LOG’.

__init__(instrument, data_handler)[source]¶
get_time()[source]¶

Query the overall acquisition length for the sweep.

If the sweep time is smaller than needed for the current RBW/VBW settings, sweep time is ignored. If sweep time is longer than necessary for the current RBW/VBW settings, VBW is lowered internally to meet the requested sweep time. The VBW is lowered internally and won’t be represented in the VBW settings.

Returns:

The current sweep time in seconds.

set_time(value)[source]¶

Set the overall acquisition length for the sweep.

If the sweep time is smaller than needed for the current RBW/VBW settings, sweep time is ignored. If sweep time is longer than necessary for the current RBW/VBW settings, VBW is lowered internally to meet the requested sweep time. The VBW is lowered internally and won’t be represented in the VBW settings.

Parameters:

value – Sweep time in seconds.

The reference level.
